utterances.text: You've been asked about what political leaders you may have met on the other side, i.e., the Croat side. Isn't it correct that you spoke to the mayor of Vitez --

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- and a gentleman called Mr. Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would refer now to your penultimate paragraph on page 1 of your report, where you make a statement regarding the apparent aims of the Croats in Vitez. Could you, sir, just explain a little further how you reached the conclusion that you state in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD
utterances.text: The conclusion that I reached there was largely distilled from the conversation that I had with Mr. Santic, where he had set out, I think very clearly, what the Croatian political objectives were, and he said very clearly what they had been attempting to do, what he believed ought to happen was that the International Community should form a buffer between Zenica and Vitez and that the populations should be balanced with a majority of Croats or, indeed, just Croats on the Vitez side and Muslims on the Zenica side, and that once that had happened, then they could implement the Vance Plan because they could have democracy, as he put it, elections, which would demonstrate, because of the way the populations were then balanced, what people wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McLeod.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours. Mr. President, if I may, sir, I would like to formally move into evidence Exhibit 393, which is the report prepared by Mr. McLeod.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Any objection? No objection. It is admitted into evidence. I have one question, Mr. McLeod. It's about your meeting with [redacted] when you went to Ahmici. Actually, I take up the question which was put to you by Counsel Slokovic-Glumac, and I have the feeling that part of the question was not answered. You went with Mr. [redacted] and an ambassador and other people to visit a house. You didn't enter that house where there were corpses, burned corpses and so on, and Counsel Slokovic-Glumac asked you whether you had heard from [redacted] that he had been told by a witness that that was his family's house, his family was there, the corpses were of people belonging to his family. Did [redacted] tell you that this particular witness had spoken of his own family?

utterances.speaker: CHARLES MCLEOD
utterances.text: What [redacted] said, not to me but to the various people that were there, was that he had heard, having interviewed somebody -- I have no idea who that person was -- that they believed that in this particular house, there would be bodies of, I can assume, his family -- I'm not sure what the connection was between the person that [redacted] had spoken to and that house -- and, indeed, what he was then attempting to do was to identify the house that he had had described to him, which he did, and then in that house, as evidenced, I think, by what various people saw and the video footage, they found some bodies. I thought that for the benefit of my mental health, I wouldn't actually go and have a look for myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you so much for giving evidence in court, Mr. McLeod. You may now be released.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: This is the close of the rebuttal case. You don't have any more witnesses. We may now then call Vlatko Kupreskic as a rejoinder witness, only on the rebuttal evidence. Counsel Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can say to you that the Defence of Vlatko Kupreskic will not call Vlatko Kupreskic to the stand again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. So we are now left only then with the court witness who is coming tomorrow, I understand, and is not here in The Hague. Yes, Counsel Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have been informed by the witnesses unit that this witness should arrive in The Hague tonight. We shall try to establish contact with that witness tonight in order to interview him, which is necessary; however, if the witness arrives too late tonight in The Hague, and if we are not in a position to talk to him, then we would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to postpone this witness's testimony tomorrow. It can take place tomorrow, but perhaps later, after the break, so that we could have contact with the witness before that. However, we do hope that we will be able to talk to the witness tonight and that it won't be necessary for any postponement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: First of all, let me ask you whether you confirm that this is the only rejoinder witness the Defence is calling. So you don't have any witnesses, any other witnesses. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: I do not, Mr. President. That is the only witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. Since you need some time to interview the witness, I think we could start tomorrow, say, at 10.00 or 10.30. So you would have some time in the morning. What do you prefer, 10.00 or 10.30? Shall we say 10.15?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: 10.30, that is what we would really prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good. We will adjourn now until tomorrow at 10.30. Counsel Radovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would just like to put a question to the Prosecutor. Could he finally state his views on whether his case has finally been completed and concluded now and that he has no further witnesses or material evidence? Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that we have no further witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Please, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, could you please allow me to inform the Court that we are going to have two witnesses after all but both will be very brief. One is (redacted) and the other one is Liljana Sapina; both will be related to the statement made here by (redacted). Tomorrow, we are going to present a report on the interview that was held with them, and we are going to give this to our colleague, the Prosecutor. This other witness will not be heard as an expert witness but as a fact witness related to the army and the functioning of the army at that time, and, indeed, it is going to be a very brief statement. We assume that on Wednesday we will have finished within two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. Wednesday, yes, it is agreed. All right. So tomorrow we just have one witness, the Court witness, starting at 10.30, and on Wednesday, two witnesses, but then again, we will start at 9.00 so that by 1.30 we must be through. There are no other matters to be discussed? All right. We will adjourn now until tomorrow at 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 11.45 a.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 5th day of October, 1999, at 10.30 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
